Entail

/en-TAYL/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Entail means to involve or require something as a necessary part or consequence.

Entail means to involve or require something as a necessary part or consequence. Adopting the retired sled dog entailed fencing the yard, doubling the food budget, and long runs in every kind of weather.

Worked Example

Two friends dreamed of opening a food truck, imagining sunny afternoons handing tacos through a window. The reality entailed far more: permits from three separate agencies, a five a.m. trip to the produce market every day, and hours of scrubbing the grill each night. None of those chores was optional; running the truck necessarily involved every one of them. What the dream would entail only became clear once the friends wrote out the full list.

Running the food truck necessarily involved permits, early markets, and nightly cleaning, and requiring those things as unavoidable parts of the plan is exactly what entail means.

How Entail Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

involve

involve: to include as a necessary part

necessitate

necessitate: to make necessary or unavoidable

Antonyms

exclude

exclude: to leave out entirely

omit

omit: to leave something out, whether by choice or by accident

How Strong Is It? — imply → dictate → entail

imply vs. entail

imply vs. entail: To imply something is only to hint that it may follow, while to entail it is to require it as a necessary consequence.

dictate vs. entail

dictate vs. entail: Entailing certain steps makes them necessary parts of a plan, but dictating them means someone in authority is commanding exactly how everything must be done.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — en-

Prefix — en-: in, into; used to form verbs

Root — tail

Root — tail: from Old French taillier, to cut, from Latin taliare

Put it together

Put it together: Entail joins en-, 'into,' with Old French taillier, 'to cut,' the same root behind tailor, detail, and retail. In old property law, to entail an estate was to cut its inheritance into one fixed line of heirs; from that came the modern sense of consequences that are cut into a choice and cannot be separated from it.

Use the root in a new word: detail

Use the root in a new word: detail: The blueprint's every detail is, by the root taillier, a small piece cut away from the whole design for a closer look.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, academic and everyday register

Entail takes a direct object or an -ing phrase: the job entails travel, the move entails packing everything by June. It states what necessarily comes with a choice, so use it for built-in requirements and consequences, never for optional extras.
